Calibration Plot of Predicted Risks

Source: R/validation_curves.R
plot_calibration.Rd

Plots the mean predicted risk of each bin against the observed event rate, with a confidence interval, the diagonal of perfect calibration, and the calibration slope and intercept of each model in the subtitle (binary outcomes). See [calibration_table()] for the definitions, the Surv outcomes and the handling of competing events.

Usage

plot_calibration(
  truth,
  pred,
  horizon = NULL,
  bins = 10,
  strategy = c("quantile", "uniform"),
  event_level = c("second", "first"),
  conf_level = 0.95,
  smooth = FALSE
)

Arguments

truth

The outcome: 0/1, logical, a two-level factor, or a right-censored [survival::Surv()] object.

pred

Predicted risks (probabilities of the event, by `horizon` for Surv outcomes): a numeric vector, or a named list or data frame with one element per model.

horizon

For a Surv `truth`, the time at which the predicted risks apply.

bins

Number of bins (default `10`).

strategy

`"quantile"` (default; bins of equal size) or `"uniform"` (equal-width bins of the predicted risk).

event_level

For a factor `truth`: `"second"` (default, as `glm()`) or `"first"` level is the event.

conf_level

Level of the confidence intervals (default `0.95`): Wilson for binary, log-log Kaplan-Meier for Surv outcomes.

smooth

Also draw a loess smooth of the observed event on the predicted risk, for a binary outcome (default `FALSE`).

Value

A `ggplot2` object.

See also

[calibration_table()], [decision_curve()]

Examples

set.seed(1)
p <- runif(500)
y <- rbinom(500, 1, p)
plot_calibration(y, list(correct = p, overconfident = plogis(2 * qlogis(pmin(pmax(p, .01), .99)))))
